correctness.rationale: The equilibrium existence and positive uniqueness follow via maximum/minimum comparison; linearization exactly cancels instantaneous mortality in the logistic term and leads to a cyclic Fourier scalar quasipolynomial. At delay zero all roots are strictly left; right-half-plane roots are bounded so first loss crosses the imaginary axis. The two frequency signs and all phase wraps were compared. For n=3 a strictly convex G proves no transverse-first mode, and for n=4 a strictly concave F gives one interior switch q*. Derivative Re z_s is strictly positive at first crossings; the q<q* region has q<1/sqrt(2) so every subsequent rotating crossing is rightward. For q>=q*, the synchronous scalar crossing persists in the right half-plane for all later delays. An explicit q=1/2 witness and standard-library modal numerical tests passed. No inference of global nonlinear behavior is made.

Relevant neural ring work covers analogous mode competition but different characteristic terms. Semantic published-finding corpus plus textual bibliographic searches for parameter and model aliases did not reveal a covering claim. This judgment has explicit residual risk of a more general delayed-circulant modal theorem.

value.rationale: The unresolved role of intermediate dispersal and network topology in loss-bearing delayed population models makes the order of synchronous and nonuniform instability a structurally natural question. The theorem gives a fully explicit all-strength threshold, a smallest cyclic topology supporting rotating-first destabilization, a unique transition, and a concrete interval where monitoring only spatial averages misses a growing transverse perturbation. The narrow ring family is inherent to the biological mechanism, not an arbitrary one-off slice.
